_meta.status: Oct 28 clinical anchors from OCT28_MEDICAL_ANSWERS. Textbook anchors (ATLS / TCCC / NREMT / PHTLS). Needs sign-off from a certified medic before Nov 4.
_meta.basis: ATLS / TCCC / NREMT / PHTLS textbook anchors. Fields tagged TUNE are adjustable for gameplay.

baselines.subject: Josh, healthy 28M before the crash
baselines.tidalVolume_mL_note: about 550 mL at 80 kg, minute ventilation about 7.7 L/min
baselines.weight_note: Keep 80 kg. Blood volume 5,600 mL. Do NOT show weight to the player anywhere in UI. Josh says about 175 pounds if asked (patient prompt data, Oct 29 voice).

crashStressOffset.note: Applied at call start, separate from blood loss. Fades as analgesia takes effect.

shockClasses.basis: ATLS classes from 5,600 mL blood volume

interpolationAnchors_TUNE.note: Engine anchors. Interpolate linearly between rows by loss percent.

compensationOrder: 2. Peripheral vasoconstriction: pale, cool skin, cap refill over 2 s
3. Pulse pressure narrows. DBP rises while SBP holds.
5. Mental status declines: anxious, then confused, then lethargic
6. SBP falls, Class III. This is the late sign.
7. Radial pulse lost. Engine rule only, not a teaching claim: rough heuristic SBP below about 80.
8. Decompensation: HR falls before arrest. Bradycardia in a bleeding patient is ominous, not improvement. Then PEA.

radialPulseRule.note: Engine rule only, not a teaching claim. Rough heuristic.

shockIndexFlag.betaBlocker: Suppress the HR rise by about 60 percent, TUNE. Shock index then looks falsely reassuring, and the FTO should point that out.

effectTokens._tag: TUNE - drug effect-token map. Change at peak effect, at the standard dose. Scale linearly with dose divided by standard dose up to 2 times. Above that apply toxicity flags from drugs.json.
effectTokens.fluidsNote: Fluids are NOT tokens. Model them explicitly: 1,000 mL crystalloid adds +1,000 mL intravascular immediately, then decays to about 250 mL retained over 60 min. Blood products stay about 90 percent intravascular.

bleedRates_mL_per_min._tag: TUNE - mL/min at baseline MAP 93. All pressure-scaled except capillary: rate = base x (currentMAP / 93).

femoral_bike_down.note: Partial laceration. Partials often bleed more than complete transections because the vessel cannot retract and spasm. Untreated: Class II at about 1.5 min, Class III at about 3 min, Class IV at about 4 min, arrest window at about 5-6 min. Tourniquet within about 3 min keeps him out of Class IV.
